observations:
Torah #144 is a brief, single-polarity-contrast teaching (6 lines). It contains exactly two thematic domains — both of which are fully captured by Package 1 and Package 2 proposed in torah_144_packages.json:

  Package 1 (good): הַצַּדִּיק וְהַחַיִּים — the Tzaddik, always alive, master of desire.
  Package 2 (evil): תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה וְהַמָּוֶת — the desire-chaser, identified as dead.

The teaching's sole structural move is a binary contrast:
  [Package 2: evil] — The desire-driven person IS death.
  vs.
  [Package 1: good] — The Tzaddik IS always alive.

No third or fourth domain is developed. The teaching does not introduce:
  - A distinct epistemological domain (no wisdom/sekhel cluster)
  - A distinct ritual domain (prayer, Torah, etc. are not discussed)
  - A distinct cosmic/kabbalistic domain (no sefirot, no divine names)
  - A distinct evil counterpart beyond the desire-chaser already in Package 2

The halakhic reference to חֶצְיוֹ לַה' וְחֶצְיוֹ לָכֶם (Pesachim 68b) is a contextual citation, not the genesis of a new conceptual cluster.

The concept of עֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם (serving God) appears twice but functions as an aspect of Package 1's 'תָּמִיד חַי' rather than forming an independent domain with 3+ bechina-connected nodes.

The good/evil mirror structure of the teaching is clean and complete within the two proposed packages:
  - Package 1 (Tzaddik = life) mirrors Package 2 (desire-chaser = death)
  - This is the entire theological argument of the teaching.

There are no 3+ node independent domains visible in the source text that are not accounted for by the two proposed packages.

Conclusion: Torah #144 yields exactly 2 packages (1 good, 1 evil), 5 proposed nodes total, 0 new packages needed beyond those already identified.
